elements.element: Audits are limited to no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause limits inspections to once “per year,” which does not unambiguously impose a rolling 12-month restriction and could permit inspections near the end and beginning of successive years.

elements.element: Customer receives at least 30 days' prior written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company.”

elements.element: Audits are conducted only during Customer's normal business hours.
elements.evidence: Inspection is expressly limited to “the Company's normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit is conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is granted to HDI's General Manager, with no independence requirement.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no confidentiality obligation applicable to the inspecting party.

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit costs when underpayment does not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires HDI to bear its inspection fees in all circumstances, which is more protective than requiring Vendor payment only up to the stated threshold.

elements.element: Customer can be required to bear audit costs only if underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause does not permit audit costs to be shifted to Customer at any underpayment level.

elements.element: Vendor and its auditor receive no direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: Although the clause refers to inspection of records, it contains no operative prohibition against direct access to Customer systems.

elements.element: Audits are limited to no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly limits the inspection right to “no more than once per year.”

elements.element: Customer receives at least 15 days' prior notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days' prior written notice, exceeding the fallback notice period.

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit costs when underpayment does not exceed 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires HDI to bear its inspection fees in all circumstances, including when underpayment does not exceed 10%.

elements.element: Customer can be required to bear audit costs only if underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause does not permit audit costs to be shifted to Customer at any underpayment level.

result.reason: The redline minimally adds the frequency cap needed to complete the fallback, while the existing notice, business-hours, and HDI-cost provisions remain effective. It does not satisfy the preferred position because “per year” is not an unambiguous rolling 12-month limit, the inspector is HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor, and there are no confidentiality or no-system-access protections.
